name: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA / Churg-Strauss)
overview: EGPA presents with severe adult-onset asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis, peripheral eosinophilia (>1,000/mcL or >10%), and necrotizing vasculitis (mononeuritis multiplex, cardiac involvement). The landmark MIRRA trial (n=136) proved that anti-IL-5 monoclonal antibody Mepolizumab (300 mg SC monthly) achieved significantly more weeks of remission (28% vs 3%; p<0.001) and allowed 44% of patients to reduce daily prednisolone to <=4 mg.
patient_plain_language: A rare autoimmune condition combining severe asthma, nasal polyps, and very high levels of allergy cells (eosinophils) that attack and inflame your blood vessels. It can cause numbness or weakness in your hands or feet (wrist or foot drop) and can affect the heart. Modern biologic injections like Mepolizumab block the allergy cells and allow patients to stop dangerous steroids.

name: Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA)
overview: ABPA is an intense hypersensitivity reaction to Aspergillus fumigatus colonizing the bronchial tree in asthma or cystic fibrosis patients. Oral Itraconazole (200 mg BID x 16 weeks) combined with Oral Corticosteroids suppresses fungal burden, reduces exacerbation rate by >50%, and clears central bronchiectasis with high-attenuation mucus (HAM) plugging. If you have asthma or cystic fibrosis, the mold sets up home in your airways. Your body releases massive amounts of allergy antibodies (IgE), causing thick brown mucus plugs and airway damage. Antifungal pills plus steroids clear the mold and calm the allergy.

name: Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome (Pickwickian Sleep Hypoventilation)
overview: OHS triad consists of Obesity (BMI >=30 kg/m2), daytime hypercapnia (arterial PaCO2 >=45 mmHg), and sleep-disordered breathing in the absence of alternative causes. Positive Airway Pressure (PAP: CPAP for comorbid severe OSA, or Non-Invasive Bi-level PAP for persistent hypoventilation) corrects hypercapnia, eliminates nocturnal hypoxia, and cuts 5-year mortality from 23% to <4% (p<0.001). Bariatric metabolic surgery provides definitive reversal.
patient_plain_language: Severe excess body weight presses down on your chest wall and diaphragm like heavy sandbags. Your breathing muscles cannot work hard enough, so carbon dioxide (waste gas) builds up in your blood during the day and night. Using a nighttime breathing machine (PAP mask) pushes air in to wash out the toxic carbon dioxide, restoring daytime energy.

name: Vocal Cord Dysfunction / Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction (ILO)
alternative_names: Vocal Cord Dysfunction / Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction (ILO)
overview: VCD/ILO involves paradoxical adduction (closure) of vocal cords during INSPIRATION, producing acute stridor, throat tightness, and air hunger that mimics severe refractory asthma. Asthma bronchodilator inhalers (albuterol) and systemic corticosteroids ARE COMPLETELY INEFFECTIVE and lead to iatrogenic toxicity. SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY (SLP) respiratory retraining and quick-release panting techniques achieve >90% symptom control.
patient_plain_language: Your vocal cords (voice box) snap tightly shut when you breathe IN, instead of opening wide to let air enter. It feels like breathing through a crushed straw and sounds like a high-pitched wheeze or squeak. It is frequently misdiagnosed as 'severe asthma', but asthma inhalers and steroids never help. Speech therapy breathing exercises train your vocal cords to stay wide open.

name: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD / Samter Triad)
overview: Samter Triad consists of Severe Eosinophilic Asthma, Recurrent Nasal Polyposis, and Acute Bronchospasm/Rhinorrhea upon ingestion of COX-1 inhibitors (aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen). Dysregulated arachidonic acid metabolism causes massive overproduction of cysteinyl leukotrienes. ASPIRIN DESENSITIZATION followed by high-dose daily aspirin maintenance (650-1300 mg/day) or Biologics (Dupilumab anti-IL-4R-alpha) restores smell and prevents polyp regrowth.
patient_plain_language: A distinctive condition combining severe asthma, aggressive nasal polyps that block your sense of smell, and a severe reaction to aspirin and ibuprofen (Advil/Aleve). Taking even a single aspirin pill causes intense asthma attacks, nasal flushing, and abdominal cramping. After sinus surgery, specialized aspirin desensitization or Dupilumab shots keeps polyps from growing back.

name: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC - Anti-Mitochondrial Antibodies)
overview: URSODEOXYCHOLIC ACID (UDCA 13-15 mg/kg/day) is the foundational first-line therapy, delaying histological progression and significantly prolonging transplant-free survival (Paris II criteria: normal bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase <1.5x ULN). In inadequate responders (~40%), adding Obeticholic Acid or Bezafibrate/PPAR agonists normalizes liver biochemistry and halts fibrosis.
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where your body's immune system slowly attacks and destroys the microscopic bile ducts inside your liver. When bile cannot drain, it backs up into liver cells and spills into your blood, causing severe full-body skin itching (pruritus) and deep exhaustion. Taking a natural bile acid pill (Ursodiol) daily protects your liver cells and prevents cirrhosis.

name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC - Large Duct Beaded Strictures)
alternative_names: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC - Large Duct Beaded Strictures)
overview: PSC causes progressive fibrosing obliterative cholangitis of intra- and extra-hepatic bile ducts ('string-of-beads' / multifocal strictures on MRCP). 70-80% of patients have comorbid Inflammatory Bowel Disease (predominantly Ulcerative Colitis). PSC carries an intense 400-fold elevated risk of CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA (bile duct cancer). ANNUAL SURVEILLANCE with MRCP and CA 19-9, plus ANNUAL SCREENING COLONOSCOPY for colorectal cancer, is mandatory.
patient_plain_language: A chronic disease that causes inflammation, scarring, and tightening of the medium and large bile pipes inside and outside your liver. Over 70% of people with PSC also have Ulcerative Colitis. Because the scarred ducts carry a significant risk of developing bile duct cancer (cholangiocarcinoma), having a yearly MRI scan and yearly colonoscopy is absolutely essential.

name: Autoimmune Hepatitis (Type 1 Anti-SMA & Hypergammaglobulinemia)
overview: AIH is characterized by female predominance, circulating autoantibodies (Anti-Smooth Muscle Antibody / ASMA or ANA in Type 1; Anti-LKM1 in Type 2), elevated serum IgG (>1.2x ULN), and interface hepatitis on liver biopsy. COMBINATION INDUCTION THERAPY (Oral Prednisone 30 mg/day tapered to 10 mg + Azathioprine 1-2 mg/kg/day) achieves complete biochemical and histological remission in >85% of patients.
patient_plain_language: Your own immune system mistakes your liver cells for foreign invaders and attacks them, driving up liver enzymes into the hundreds or thousands. If untreated, it causes rapid cirrhosis. Taking a combination of steroid pills (Prednisone) and an immune-calming pill (Azathioprine) successfully cools down the immune attack in over 85% of people.

name: Wilson's Disease (Hepatolenticular Degeneration - Copper Overload)
overview: Autosomal recessive ATP7B mutation impairs biliary copper excretion, causing toxic copper accumulation in liver, basal ganglia (dysarthria, dystonia, parkinsonism), and cornea (Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp). CHELATION THERAPY WITH PENICILLAMINE OR TRIENTINE promotes massive urinary copper excretion, while Oral Zinc blocks intestinal copper absorption. Lifelong therapy is mandatory; abrupt discontinuation causes fatal acute liver failure.
patient_plain_language: A genetic condition where your liver cannot pump extra dietary copper into bile. Over years, toxic copper piles up inside your liver and brain, causing cirrhosis, tremors, muscle stiffness, and golden-brown copper rings around your eyes (Kayser-Fleischer rings). Daily copper-binding medicine (Trientine or Penicillamine) flushes copper out in your urine.

name: Hereditary Hemochromatosis (C282Y HFE Iron Overload)
overview: Homozygosity for C282Y mutation in the HFE gene causes uncontrolled intestinal iron absorption, leading to parenchymal iron deposition ('Bronze Diabetes', cirrhosis, dilated cardiomyopathy, and pseudogout chondrocalcinosis). THERAPEUTIC PHLEBOTOMY (removing 500 mL blood weekly or biweekly until serum ferritin reaches 50-100 mcg/L) normalizes lifespan and prevents cirrhosis if started before advanced fibrosis.
patient_plain_language: Your body absorbs far too much iron from ordinary food because of a genetic mutation in the HFE gene. The excess iron cannot be excreted, so it rusts and deposits inside your liver, heart, joints, and pancreas ('Bronze Diabetes'). The treatment is remarkably simple and natural: having a pint of blood removed (therapeutic phlebotomy) regularly until iron stores reach normal levels.

name: Gastroparesis (Delayed Gastric Emptying / Diabetic Gastroparesis)
overview: Gastroparesis presents with chronic nausea, early satiety, and postprandial vomiting without mechanical obstruction. 4-hour Gastric Emptying Scintigraphy (GES) showing >10% retention at 4 hours establishes diagnosis. METOCLOPRAMIDE (oral or nasal spray Gimoti) remains the only FDA-approved medication, improving gastric motility via 5-HT4 agonism and D2 antagonism. G-POEM (Gastric Peroral Endoscopic Myotomy) provides durable surgical pyloromyotomy.
patient_plain_language: The muscular pump of your stomach becomes sluggish and partly paralyzed (often caused by diabetes or nerve injury). Food sits in your stomach for hours without moving into your intestines, causing you to feel stuffed after just a few bites, nauseated, and vomiting undigested food eaten hours earlier. Eating small, low-fiber, blended meals helps gravity pull food down.

name: Esophageal Achalasia (Aperistalsis & Non-Relaxing LES)
overview: Loss of inhibitory myenteric ganglion cells causes absent esophageal peristalsis and failed relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter (LES). HIGH-RESOLUTION MANOMETRY (HRM utilizing Chicago Classification v4.0: integrated relaxation pressure / IRP elevated) is the diagnostic gold standard. POEM (Peroral Endoscopic Myotomy) or Laparoscopic Heller Myotomy with fundoplication provides >90% long-term dysphagia relief.
patient_plain_language: The muscular ring at the bottom of your swallowing tube (lower esophageal sphincter) stays clamped shut like a clenched fist and refuses to open when you swallow. Food and liquids pile up in your esophagus, causing severe difficulty swallowing, chest pain, and regurgitation of undigested meals. A minimally invasive procedure (POEM) cuts the tight muscle ring open, letting food drop freely into your stomach.

name: Zenker's Diverticulum (Killian Triangle Pharyngeal Pouch)
overview: Failure of cricopharyngeus muscle relaxation causes high intraluminal pressure, herniating pharyngeal mucosa through Killian's triangle (anatomical weak spot between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus). Presents with oropharyngeal dysphagia, regurgitation of foul undigested food hours later, halitosis, and gurgling in the neck. ENDOSCOPIC CRICOPHARYNGEAL MYOTOMY (flexible or rigid endoscopic diverticulotomy / Z-POEM) achieves >90% symptom resolution.
patient_plain_language: A small outpouching or pocket forms at the back of your throat, right above your swallowing tube. Food gets trapped inside this pouch instead of going down to your stomach. Hours or days later, trapped undigested food regurgitates back into your mouth with a foul smell (halitosis) and loud gurgling noises in your neck. A quick endoscopic laser or scissor myotomy cuts the pouch wall, allowing food to slide straight down.

name: Microscopic Colitis: Collagenous Colitis (Subepithelial Band)
overview: Collagenous colitis presents with chronic, profuse, watery, non-bloody diarrhea (>4-10 bowel movements/day) with completely NORMAL-APPEARING colonic mucosa on colonoscopy. Diagnosis requires random colonic mucosal biopsies showing a thickened subepithelial collagen band (>10 micrometers). ORAL BUDESONIDE (9 mg/day x 6-8 weeks) is the gold standard Level 1 therapy, inducing clinical remission in >80-88% of patients.
patient_plain_language: A condition causing chronic, watery diarrhea (often 5 to 10 watery stools a day) where your colon appears 100% healthy and pink on colonoscopy. The inflammation is only visible under a microscope, where a thick band of collagen scar tissue lines the bowel wall. Specialized gut-targeted steroid pills (Budesonide) heal the microscopic inflammation in over 85% of people.

name: Microscopic Colitis: Lymphocytic Colitis (Intraepithelial Lymphocytes)
overview: Unlike collagenous colitis which features a thick collagen band, Lymphocytic Colitis is characterized by marked intraepithelial lymphocytosis (>=20 lymphocytes per 100 surface epithelial cells) with normal collagen thickness. Presents with identical severe watery diarrhea and normal endoscopic appearance. ORAL BUDESONIDE (9 mg/day) achieves clinical response in >85%; high overlap with Celiac Disease (serological screening mandatory).
patient_plain_language: Similar to collagenous colitis, lymphocytic colitis causes persistent, watery diarrhea with completely normal-looking bowel lining during a colonoscopy. Under the microscope, large armies of immune lymphocytes crowd between your intestinal cells. Taking gut-targeted Budesonide capsules clears the immune cells, and testing for celiac disease is mandatory.

name: Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency (EPI - Severe Steatorrhea)
overview: EPI results from destruction of >90% of pancreatic acinar tissue (chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, pancreatic resection), causing maldigestion of fats and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K). Fecal Elastase-1 (<100 mcg/g stool) confirms severe EPI. PANCREATIC ENZYME REPLACEMENT THERAPY (PERT: minimum 40,000-50,000 USP lipase units per full meal) taken DURING meals normalizes fat absorption and halts debilitating weight loss.
patient_plain_language: Your pancreas has lost its ability to manufacture digestive enzymes (lipase, protease, amylase). Because dietary fats cannot be digested, they pass straight through into your stool, causing pale, greasy, foul-smelling stools that float and stick to the toilet bowl, along with weight loss. Taking natural pancreatic enzyme capsules with every meal restores normal digestion.

name: Chronic Calcific Pancreatitis (Intractable Pain & Duct Stones)
alternative_names: Chronic Calcific Pancreatitis (Intractable Pain & Duct Stones)
overview: Chronic irreversible inflammation causes acinar atrophy, periductal fibrosis, and intraductal calcified stones, resulting in debilitating abdominal pain, EPI, and pancreatogenic diabetes (Type 3c). Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL) combined with ERCP stone extraction and stenting relieves ductal hypertension; surgical drainage (Frey or Puestow procedure) provides superior long-term pain relief over endoscopy for large duct disease.
patient_plain_language: Permanent, irreversible scarring and calcium stones form inside the drainage ducts of your pancreas (most often from heavy alcohol use, smoking, or genetics). The blocked ducts build up extreme pressure, causing severe, boring abdominal pain that shoots straight through to your back. Quitting smoking and alcohol is mandatory, and shock-wave therapy or surgery can remove the stones to relieve the pressure.

name: Budd-Chiari Syndrome (Hepatic Venous Outflow Obstruction)
overview: Thrombosis or obstruction of the hepatic veins or suprahepatic IVC leads to extreme hepatic sinusoidal congestion, ischemic centrilobular necrosis, and acute liver failure or cirrhosis. Over 80% of patients have an underlying myeloproliferative neoplasm (JAK2 V617F mutation). STEPWISE MANAGEMENT STRATEGY: 1) Lifelong therapeutic anticoagulation; 2) Angioplasty/stenting for short stenosis; 3) Early TIPS (Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt) if medical failure, yielding >85% 5-year survival.
patient_plain_language: A rare and dangerous blood clot forms in the main drainage veins leaving your liver (hepatic veins). Because blood can enter the liver through arteries but cannot drain out, the liver swells with trapped blood like an over-filled water balloon, causing rapid abdominal fluid buildup (ascites), liver pain, and liver failure. Immediate blood thinners and an internal vein bypass stent (TIPS) save the liver.

name: Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis (SBP - Ascitic PMN >=250/mcL)
overview: SBP is an acute bacterial infection of ascitic fluid without an evident intra-abdominal surgical source. Diagnostic paracentesis is MANDATORY in any cirrhotic patient hospitalized with ascites. Ascitic Polymorphonuclear (PMN) count >=250 cells/mcL mandates immediate empiric IV Ceftriaxone (2 g/day x 5 days) COMBINED WITH INTRAVENOUS ALBUMIN (1.5 g/kg at diagnosis, followed by 1.0 g/kg on day 3), which reduces hepatorenal syndrome from 33% to 10% and mortality from 29% to 10% (p=0.01).
patient_plain_language: A severe, life-threatening bacterial infection that develops spontaneously inside the fluid pool in your belly (ascites) in patients with liver cirrhosis. It may cause mild fever, abdominal discomfort, or simply sudden confusion. Tapping the belly fluid with a thin needle (paracentesis) is urgent; treatment requires IV antibiotics plus human albumin protein infusions to protect your kidneys.

name: Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS-AKI - Refractory Vasoplegia)
overview: HRS-AKI is functional renal failure in advanced cirrhosis driven by extreme splanchnic arterial vasodilation and renal vasoconstriction, occurring without structural parenchymal kidney damage. In the phase 3 CONFIRM trial (n=300), TERLIPRESSIN (IV bolus or continuous infusion) COMBINED WITH IV ALBUMIN achieved significantly higher verified HRS reversal (32% vs 17%; p=0.006) and lowered dialysis dependence compared to placebo.
patient_plain_language: A severe complication of advanced liver disease where your kidneys shut down, not because the kidneys themselves are diseased, but because extreme dilation of belly blood vessels starves the kidneys of blood pressure. Stopping all water pills and infusing a specialized vasoconstrictor drug (Terlipressin) with concentrated Albumin protein forces blood back into the kidneys while waiting for a liver transplant.

name: Hepatic Encephalopathy (West Haven Neuropsychiatric Staging)
overview: Impaired hepatic clearance and portosystemic shunting allow neurotoxins (ammonia) to cross the blood-brain barrier, causing astrocyte swelling and cognitive impairment. NON-ABSORBABLE DISACCHARIDE LACTULOSE (titrated to achieve 2-3 soft bowel movements daily) is first-line therapy. RIFAXIMIN (550 mg BID; non-absorbable rifamycin antibiotic) added to lactulose reduces recurrence by 58% (p<0.001) and hospitalizations by 50%. PROTEIN RESTRICTION IS STRICTLY HARMFUL.
patient_plain_language: When the liver is severely scarred or bypassed by shunts, it cannot filter ammonia and digestive toxins produced by gut bacteria. These toxins reach your brain, causing sleepiness during the day, insomnia at night, confusion, and a flapping hand tremor (asterixis). Taking Lactulose syrup (to produce 2 to 3 soft bowel movements a day) and Rifaximin pills flushes the toxins out through your intestines.

name: Eosinophilic Esophagitis (EoE - Trachealization & Food Impaction)
overview: EoE is a chronic Th2-mediated allergic inflammation of the esophagus characterized by mucosal eosinophilia (>=15 eosinophils per high-power field). In the pivotal phase 3 LIBERTY EoE TREET trial (n=321), subcutaneous DUPILUMAB (300 mg weekly) achieved histological remission (<6 eosinophils/HPF) in 60% vs 5% placebo (p<0.001) and significantly improved Dysphagia Symptom Questionnaire scores. Swallowed topical fluticasone/budesonide or 6-food elimination diet (6FED) are alternative first-line therapies.
patient_plain_language: An allergic inflammation inside your swallowing tube (esophagus) triggered by common foods (most often cow's milk and wheat). Allergy cells (eosinophils) pack into the tissue, making the tube stiff, narrow, and ribbed like a vacuum cleaner hose (trachealization). Food—especially steak, dry chicken, or dense bread—suddenly gets stuck midway down your chest, causing a terrifying choking blockage.

name: Severe Erosive Reflux Esophagitis (Los Angeles Grade C/D)
alternative_names: Severe Erosive Reflux Esophagitis (Los Angeles Grade C/D)
overview: Severe erosive esophagitis (LA Grade C with confluent mucosal breaks >5 mm across folds, or LA Grade D involving >=75% of circumference) carries high risk for peptic stricture, severe ulcer bleeding, and Barrett's metaplasia. HIGH-DOSE PROTON PUMP INHIBITOR (PPI BID x 8-12 weeks) is mandatory, achieving mucosal healing in >85-90%. REPEAT SURVEILLANCE ENDOSCOPY AT 8-12 WEEKS IS MANDATORY to verify complete mucosal healing and rule out occult Barrett's esophagus or dysplasia.
patient_plain_language: Stomach acid and bile splash backward into your lower esophagus with such harsh intensity that they burn deep, raw, bleeding ulcers across the delicate pink lining. It causes agonizing burning in your chest (heartburn), pain when swallowing, and can heal into tight scars (strictures) or precancerous changes (Barrett's). Taking strong acid-blocking medicine twice daily for 2 to 3 months is necessary to allow the ulcers to heal.

name: Gastric Antral Vascular Ectasia (GAVE - 'Watermelon Stomach')
overview: GAVE presents with longitudinal red stripes radiating from the pylorus ('watermelon stomach') or diffuse punctate spots, consisting of ectatic mucosal capillaries with fibrin thrombi. Highly associated with systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) and cirrhosis. Unlike portal hypertensive gastropathy, GAVE DOES NOT RESPOND TO PORTAL PRESSURE LOWERING (TIPS OR BETA-BLOCKERS ARE INEFFECTIVE). ENDOSCOPIC ARGON PLASMA COAGULATION (APC) or Radiofrequency Ablation (RFA) is the primary therapy, eliminating transfusion dependence in >75%.
patient_plain_language: The tiny microscopic blood vessels inside the lower part of your stomach (antrum) become enlarged, fragile, and twisted, forming distinctive red stripes that look like the stripes on a watermelon rind ('Watermelon Stomach'). These fragile vessels constantly ooze microscopic amounts of blood into your stomach, leading to severe chronic anemia and fatigue. Burning the vessels closed with a gentle beam of argon gas during an endoscopy stops the bleeding.

name: Dieulafoy's Lesion (Submucosal Caliber-Persistent Arterial Bleed)
overview: A Dieulafoy lesion is a developmental vascular anomaly consisting of an abnormally large, tortuous, caliber-persistent submucosal artery (1-3 mm diameter) that erodes through overlying mucosa without prior ulceration, typically on the gastric lesser curvature (within 6 cm of GE junction). Presents with massive, recurrent, life-threatening hematemesis. ENDOSCOPIC MECHANICAL THERAPY (HEMOCLIP APPLICATION OR ENDOSCOPIC BAND LIGATION) achieves >90-95% primary hemostasis and superior re-bleeding prevention compared to injection monotherapy.
patient_plain_language: A surprisingly dangerous, abnormally thick artery running just beneath the surface of your stomach wall. Because it is unusually large and does not narrow down into tiny capillaries like normal vessels, even tiny friction can cause it to wear through the stomach lining. It bursts like a tiny punctured garden hose, causing sudden, massive vomiting of bright red blood. Putting microscopic metal clips or tight rubber bands on the artery during endoscopy seals it shut permanently.

name: Minimal Change Disease (Nephrotic Foot Process Effacement)
alternative_names: Minimal Change Disease (Nephrotic Foot Process Effacement)
overview: MCD is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children and causes ~15% in adults. Light microscopy appears completely normal, while electron microscopy reveals diffuse podocyte foot process effacement. HIGH-DOSE ORAL CORTICOSTEROIDS (Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day or 60 mg/m2/day x 4-16 weeks) induce complete remission of proteinuria in >90% of children and >75-80% of adults. Calcineurin inhibitors or Rituximab for frequent relapsers.
patient_plain_language: The tiny microscopic filters in your kidneys (glomeruli) look completely normal under a standard light microscope, but their delicate cellular foot pads (podocytes) have flattened out, allowing massive amounts of protein to leak into your urine. Losing protein causes full-body swelling (especially around your eyes and legs). Fortunately, the filters are remarkably sensitive to steroid pills (Prednisone), which heal the foot pads and stop the leak.

name: Primary Membranous Nephropathy (Anti-PLA2R Antibodies)
overview: Autoantibodies against the M-type Phospholipase A2 Receptor (Anti-PLA2R; present in 70-80%) deposit subepithelially, forming the classic 'spike-and-dome' appearance on silver stain. The landmark MENTOR trial (n=130) proved that RITUXIMAB (1,000 mg on days 1 and 15) was non-inferior to cyclosporine at 12 months and vastly superior at 24 months in maintaining complete or partial remission (60% vs 20%; p<0.001) with significantly fewer adverse events.
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where your immune system makes specific antibodies (Anti-PLA2R) that attack the outer wall of your kidney filters. The antibodies form thick clumps and spikes, causing massive amounts of protein to spill into your urine. Measuring these antibodies in a simple blood test tracks your disease, and targeted antibody-clearing infusions (Rituximab) cure the inflammation without harsh chemotherapy.

name: Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS - APOL1 Podocytopathy)
overview: FSGS is characterized by sclerosis affecting segments of some (focal) glomeruli, driven by podocyte injury (APOL1 high-risk variants G1/G2 in individuals of African ancestry, circulating permeability factors, or genetic slit-diaphragm mutations). Primary FSGS with nephrotic syndrome requires high-dose corticosteroids (Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day for minimum 16 weeks) or Calcineurin Inhibitors (Tacrolimus/Cyclosporine). Genetic or secondary FSGS (hyperfiltration from obesity, solitary kidney) DOES NOT RESPOND TO IMMUNOSUPPRESSION.
patient_plain_language: Scar tissue forms in scattered patches (focal) and in small segments of your kidney filters. Because the damaged filter walls cannot seal, protein leaks into your urine and healthy kidney tissue slowly gets replaced by scars. It is crucial to determine whether your FSGS is autoimmune (which needs steroid pills) or caused by kidney strain and high blood pressure (which needs blood pressure pills and weight loss, not steroids).

name: IgA Nephropathy (Berger's Disease - Synpharyngitic Hematuria)
overview: IgA Nephropathy is the most common primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, caused by galactose-deficient IgA1 (Gd-IgA1) forming mesangial immune complexes. Classic presentation is 'synpharyngitic hematuria' (gross red/cola-colored urine developing CONCURRENTLY within 24-48 hours of an upper respiratory infection). Maximal optimized supportive care (ACEi/ARB, SGLT2i Dapagliflozin, and endothelin blocker) is foundational; targeted-release oral budesonide (Nefecon) or reduced-dose oral methylprednisolone with antibiotic prophylaxis (TESTING trial, n=503) cuts 5-year renal failure risk by >40%.
patient_plain_language: The most common kidney filter disease in the world. Your body makes an unusual form of an antibody called IgA that gets trapped in the central tissue (mesangium) of your kidney filters. The hallmark sign is noticing painless dark, cola-colored urine during the exact same 1 to 2 days that you catch a sore throat or cold. Taking blood pressure pills (ACE inhibitors and SGLT2 inhibitors) shields your kidney filters from pressure damage.

name: Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis (PSGN - Latent Subepithelial Humps)
overview: PSGN occurs after Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus infection (pharyngitis 1-3 weeks prior, or impetigo 3-6 weeks prior). Classic nephritic triad: gross hematuria ('tea-colored' urine), periorbital edema, and hypertension. Hallmark laboratory findings: PROFOUNDLY DEPRESSED SERUM COMPLEMENT C3 with normal C4, and elevated anti-streptolysin O (ASO) or anti-DNase B titers. Management is ENTIRELY SUPPORTIVE (fluid and salt restriction, loop diuretics for volume overload). Over 95% of children and 75% of adults recover completely without immunosuppression.
patient_plain_language: An immune reaction in your kidneys that strikes 1 to 3 weeks AFTER a strep throat infection (or 3 to 6 weeks after a strep skin sore). It is NOT an active kidney infection; rather, your body's leftover immune complexes deposit in the kidneys, causing tea-colored urine, puffy eyes, and high blood pressure. In over 95% of people, the condition heals completely on its own with temporary salt restriction and water pills.

name: Lupus Nephritis (ISN/RPS Class IV Diffuse Proliferative)
alternative_names: Lupus Nephritis (ISN/RPS Class IV Diffuse Proliferative)
overview: Class IV proliferative lupus nephritis carries the highest risk of end-stage renal disease. The landmark BLISS-LN trial (n=448) proved that adding B-cell activating factor inhibitor BELIMUMAB (10 mg/kg IV monthly) to standard induction therapy (Mycophenolate Mofetil + Glucocorticoids) achieved significantly higher Primary Efficacy Renal Response (43% vs 32%; p=0.031) and reduced renal-related death by 49%. Alternative induction is the Euro-Lupus IV Cyclophosphamide protocol.
patient_plain_language: Lupus (SLE) causes your immune system to attack and severely inflame your kidney filters, causing protein and blood to leak into your urine. Diffuse proliferative (Class IV) is the most aggressive form, requiring strong immune-calming medicines. Combining Mycophenolate pills with monthly Belimumab biologic infusions calms the attack and preserves your kidneys without harsh old-school chemotherapy.

name: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD - Tolvaptan GDMT)

overview: ADPKD (PKD1 on chromosome 16 in 78%, PKD2 on chromosome 4 in 15%) causes progressive development of thousands of fluid-filled cysts, destroying renal parenchyma and causing ESRD by age 55-60. Drinking large amounts of water (3 to 4 liters a day) and taking a targeted pill called Tolvaptan blocks the hormone that feeds cyst growth.

name: Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type 1 dRTA - Alkaline Urine pH >5.5)
alternative_names: Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type 1 dRTA - Alkaline Urine pH >5.5)
overview: Type 1 dRTA is impaired alpha-intercalated cell H+-ATPase / H+/K+-ATPase excretion in the collecting duct, preventing normal urine acidification. Diagnostic hallmark: NORMAL ANION GAP METABOLIC ACIDOSIS WITH INAPPROPRIATELY ALKALINE URINE (URINE pH >5.5) IN THE PRESENCE OF SYSTEMIC ACIDOSIS. Chronic buffering leads to severe hypercalciuria, bilateral nephrocalcinosis, recurrent calcium phosphate kidney stones, and severe hypokalemia. ORAL POTASSIUM CITRATE or sodium bicarbonate completely corrects acidosis and prevents stone recurrence.
patient_plain_language: The tiny microscopic pumps in the collecting tubes of your kidneys cannot pump acid out into your urine. Because acid builds up in your blood, your bones dissolve to release calcium to buffer the acid. This calcium pours into your urine, causing recurrent kidney stones and calcified kidneys (nephrocalcinosis). Taking daily potassium citrate alkalizing powder neutralizes the acid and completely stops stones from forming.

name: Proximal Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type 2 pRTA - Fanconi Syndrome)
alternative_names: Proximal Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type 2 pRTA - Fanconi Syndrome)
overview: Type 2 pRTA is defective proximal tubule bicarbonate reabsorption (Na+/HCO3- cotransporter NBCe1). Usually part of generalized proximal tubule dysfunction (FANCONI SYNDROME: glucosuria with normal blood sugar, phosphaturia, aminoaciduria, and hypouricemia). Unlike Type 1, the distal collecting duct functions normally: when serum bicarbonate drops below tubular threshold, URINE CAN BE FULLY ACIDIFIED (URINE pH <5.5). Massive alkali doses (10-20 mEq/kg/day) plus potassium and phosphate are required; nephrocalcinosis is RARE.
patient_plain_language: The front filtering tubes of your kidneys (proximal tubules) fail to reabsorb bicarbonate, spilling it into your urine. Often, they also spill sugar (even though your blood sugar is normal), phosphate, and amino acids—a condition called Fanconi syndrome. Losing phosphate weakens your bones (rickets or osteomalacia). Taking high doses of bicarbonate plus phosphate and vitamin D restores healthy bones.

name: Hyperkalemic Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type 4 RTA - Hypoaldosteronism)
alternative_names: Hyperkalemic Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type 4 RTA - Hypoaldosteronism)
overview: Type 4 RTA is the MOST COMMON RTA, caused by aldosterone deficiency or collecting duct resistance (hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism in diabetic nephropathy, or drug-induced by ACEi, ARB, spironolactone, trimethoprim, heparin, NSAIDs). Hallmark finding: NORMAL ANION GAP METABOLIC ACIDOSIS COMBINED WITH PERSISTENT HYPERKALEMIA (serum potassium >5.0-5.5 mEq/L). Hyperkalemia directly inhibits renal cortical ammoniagenesis, impairing NH4+ excretion. FLUDROCORTISONE (0.05-0.2 mg daily) or Loop/Thiazide Diuretics corrects hyperkalemia and acidosis.
patient_plain_language: The most common kidney tubular acid condition, frequently occurring in individuals with diabetes or mild kidney disease. Your adrenal glands make too little aldosterone hormone, or your kidney tubes ignore it. Without aldosterone, your kidneys cannot excrete potassium or acid, causing potassium to climb dangerously high in your blood. Water pills (diuretics) or a tiny hormone replacement pill (Fludrocortisone) lowers potassium and restores balance.

name: Calcium Oxalate Nephrolithiasis (Hypercalciuria & Hypocitraturia)
overview: Calcium oxalate accounts for ~75-80% of all nephrolithiasis, radiopaque on X-ray/CT. Medical prevention based on 24-hour urine metabolic profile: 1) High fluid intake (>2.5-3.0 L/day); 2) NORMAL DIETARY CALCIUM (1,000-1,200 mg/day; dietary calcium restriction is HARMFUL as it increases free oxalate absorption); 3) Dietary sodium restriction (<2,000 mg/day); 4) THIAZIDE DIURETICS (Chlorthalidone 25-50 mg daily) to decrease urinary calcium excretion; 5) POTASSIUM CITRATE for hypocitraturia.
patient_plain_language: The most common type of kidney stone (accounting for 80% of stones). Calcium binds with oxalate in your urine, crystallizing into sharp, jagged stones that lodge in your kidney tubes. Counterintuitively, cutting calcium from your diet makes stones WORSE because dietary calcium is needed in your gut to trap oxalate and flush it out. Drinking 3 liters of water daily and taking potassium citrate or a thiazide pill prevents new stones.

name: Uric Acid Nephrolithiasis (Radiolucent Stones & Alkalinization)
overview: Uric acid stones (~10% of stones) are INVISIBLE ON STANDARD X-RAY (RADIOLUCENT) but readily detected on non-contrast CT. The primary driving pathophysiology is PERSISTENTLY ACIDIC URINE (URINE pH <5.5), where uric acid is insoluble (pKa 5.35). ORAL CHEMOLYSIS (URINARY ALKALINIZATION WITH POTASSIUM CITRATE targeting urine pH 6.5-7.0) COMPLETELY DISSOLVES EXISTING URIC ACID STONES without requiring surgery. ALLOPURINOL is added if hyperuricosuria or hyperuricemia is present.
patient_plain_language: Kidney stones made of crystallized uric acid. Unlike calcium stones, uric acid stones are completely invisible on regular X-rays (radiolucent). They form almost exclusively because your urine is too acidic (pH below 5.5). The most remarkable fact about these stones is that they can be completely dissolved like sugar in hot tea simply by taking potassium citrate powder to make your urine alkaline (pH 6.5 to 7.0), completely avoiding surgery.

name: Struvite Infection Stones (Triple Phosphate Staghorn Calculi)
alternative_names: Struvite Infection Stones (Triple Phosphate Staghorn Calculi)
overview: Struvite stones (magnesium ammonium phosphate / triple phosphate) form EXCLUSIVELY in the presence of UREASE-PRODUCING BACTERIA (Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella, Morganella, Pseudomonas). Bacterial urease hydrolyzes urea into ammonia and carbon dioxide, driving urine pH >7.2-8.0 and precipitating struvite and carbonate apatite. Struvite stones form massive branching 'staghorn calculi' that fill the entire renal pelvis. COMPLETE SURGICAL REMOVAL (PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROLITHOTOMY / PCNL) COMBINED WITH CULTURE-SPECIFIC ANTIBIOTICS IS MANDATORY; residual fragments inevitably cause fatal sepsis.
patient_plain_language: Dangerous 'infection stones' that grow rapidly into giant branching antlers (staghorn stones) that fill your entire kidney plumbing system. They form exclusively when certain bacteria (like Proteus) produce an enzyme called urease, turning your urine strongly alkaline and creating magnesium-ammonium-phosphate crystals. Because the stone is literally made of living bacteria, antibiotics cannot penetrate it; keyhole surgery (PCNL) through your back to remove every last grain of stone is required to prevent life-threatening blood infections.

name: Interstitial Cystitis / Bladder Pain Syndrome (Hunner Lesions)
alternative_names: Interstitial Cystitis / Bladder Pain Syndrome (Hunner Lesions)
overview: IC/BPS is chronic pelvic pain, pressure, or discomfort perceived to be related to the urinary bladder, accompanied by persistent urinary urgency and extreme frequency (>10-30 voids/day) in the absence of infection. Phenotyped into Non-Hunner IC vs Hunner Lesion IC (erythematous velvety mucosal patches with central scar on cystoscopy). MULTIMODAL THERAPY: 1) Self-care and dietary modification; 2) Pelvic floor physical therapy (MYOFASCIAL RELEASE - KEGEL EXERCISES ARE STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED); 3) Oral Amitriptyline, Pentosan Polysulfate Sodium (PPS), or Cimetidine; 4) Endoscopic fulguration/triamcinolone injection for Hunner lesions.
patient_plain_language: A chronic, agonizing bladder condition causing burning pelvic pain, pressure, and needing to urinate 20 to 40 times a day and night, even though urine cultures show zero bacteria. The protective lining of your bladder wall is thinned or inflamed, and some patients develop velvety red ulcers (Hunner's lesions). Avoiding acidic foods (coffee, citrus, tomatoes), doing relaxing pelvic floor physical therapy (never Kegel tightening), and taking bladder-protective pills brings lasting relief.

name: Anti-Glomerular Basement Membrane Disease (Goodpasture Syndrome)
overview: Autoantibodies directed against the non-collagenous domain of the alpha-3 chain of Type IV collagen [alpha3(IV)NC1] cause necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage (Goodpasture triad: RPGN, pulmonary hemorrhage, anti-GBM antibodies). IMMEDIATE TRIPLE INDUCTION THERAPY IS MANDATORY: 1) Intensive Plasma Exchange (Plasmapheresis: 4 L exchanges daily or alternate-day for 14 days or until anti-GBM undetectable); 2) Oral Cyclophosphamide (2 mg/kg/day x 3 months); 3) High-dose Corticosteroids (pulse IV methylprednisolone 1 g x 3 days then oral prednisone). Dialysis independence is achieved in >80% if treated before serum creatinine >5.7 mg/dL or anuria.
patient_plain_language: A rare, aggressive medical emergency where your body manufactures antibodies that attack the collagen foundations in your kidney filters and your lungs (Goodpasture's syndrome). It causes rapid kidney failure within days and can cause you to cough up blood. Immediate blood filtering (plasmapheresis) to wash out the antibodies, combined with strong immune-calming pills, preserves your kidneys and saves your life if started immediately.

name: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (GPA / Wegener's PR3-ANCA)
overview: GPA is a necrotizing granulomatous small-vessel vasculitis associated with PR3-ANCA (c-ANCA in 80-90%), causing destructive upper airway lesions (saddle nose deformity, subglottic stenosis), cavitary lung nodules, and crescentic glomerulonephritis. The RAVE trial established RITUXIMAB (375 mg/m2 weekly x 4) as non-inferior to cyclophosphamide for induction and superior for relapsing disease. The landmark ADVOCATE trial (n=330) proved that oral Complement C5a Receptor Antagonist AVACOPAN (30 mg BID) replaced high-dose glucocorticoids, achieving superior sustained remission at week 52 (65.7% vs 54.9%; p=0.007) with 60% lower steroid toxicity.
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where antibodies (PR3-ANCA) inflame and destroy small blood vessels, particularly in your nose, sinuses, lungs, and kidneys. It can cause chronic bloody nasal crusts, a collapsed nasal bridge ('saddle nose'), lung cavities, and kidney inflammation. Modern treatment uses targeted B-cell clearing infusions (Rituximab) and a breakthrough steroid-sparing pill (Avacopan) that shields your kidneys without the severe side effects of high-dose prednisone.

name: Microscopic Polyangiitis (MPA - MPO-ANCA / p-ANCA)
overview: Unlike GPA, MPA is NON-GRANULOMATOUS, lacks destructive sinus/upper airway involvement, and is predominantly associated with MPO-ANCA (perinuclear p-ANCA in 70-85%). Presents with rapidly progressive necrotizing glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage. The landmark PEXIVAS trial (n=704) proved that routine plasma exchange did NOT reduce death or ESRD in severe ANCA vasculitis, and established that a REDUCED-DOSE GLUCOCORTICOID PROTOCOL was non-inferior to high-dose steroids for remission while cutting serious infections by 31% (hazard ratio 0.69; p=0.02).
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune small blood vessel inflammation that specifically attacks your kidney filters and the blood vessels in your lungs. It is driven by antibodies called MPO-ANCA (p-ANCA). Unlike its sibling disease GPA, it does not attack your nose or sinuses, but it can rapidly damage your kidneys if not treated. The landmark PEXIVAS trial proved that using a smarter, lower dose of steroid pills cures the disease just as well while saving patients from dangerous infections.

name: Rhabdomyolysis (Crush Injury & Myoglobinuric AKI)
overview: Skeletal muscle breakdown releases toxic intracellular contents (myoglobin, creatine kinase, potassium, phosphorus) into the circulation. Myoglobin induces acute kidney injury via renal vasoconstriction, direct proximal tubular cytotoxicity, and intratubular Tamm-Horsfall cast obstruction (acidic urine pH promotes cast formation). AGGRESSIVE ISOTONIC SALINE RESUSCITATION (infusing 500-1000 mL/h targeting urine output 200-300 mL/h) initiated within 6 hours of onset eliminates renal failure in >80% of patients.
patient_plain_language: Severe muscle breakdown triggered by a crush injury, intense unaccustomed exercise, prolonged immobility on a hard floor, or certain medications (like statins). Damaged muscle fibers burst, pouring dark muscle pigment (myoglobin) into your bloodstream. The pigment clogs and poisons your kidney tubes, turning your urine dark reddish-brown like iced tea. Pumping large amounts of IV fluids immediately flushes the pigment safely out of your kidneys.

name: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury (CA-AKI / CIN)
overview: CA-AKI is an abrupt decline in renal function within 48-72 hours of intravascular iodinated contrast administration. The definitive landmark PRESERVE trial (n=5,177 high-risk patients undergoing angiography) proved that INTRAVENOUS ISOTONIC 0.9% SODIUM CHLORIDE was the gold standard, and that Sodium Bicarbonate or Oral N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) provided NO BENEFIT in preventing death, dialysis, or persistent renal decline. Use of low-osmolar or iso-osmolar contrast and minimizing contrast volume (Contrast Volume / eGFR ratio <3.0) prevents injury.
patient_plain_language: A temporary decline in kidney function that can happen after receiving concentrated iodine contrast dye for a CT scan or heart catheterization. The dye temporarily narrows kidney blood vessels and causes oxygen stress. The landmark PRESERVE trial of over 5,000 patients showed that simple, regular IV saline fluid given before and after the scan protects your kidneys better than any special pills or fancy solutions.

name: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (Drug-Induced AIN - Triad Fever/Rash/Eosinophilia)
alternative_names: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (Drug-Induced AIN - Triad Fever/Rash/Eosinophilia)
overview: Drug-induced AIN accounts for 15-20% of unexplained acute kidney injury, triggered by Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs), NSAIDs, Beta-lactam antibiotics, Ciprofloxacin, or Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs). The classic triad (fever, maculopapular rash, peripheral eosinophilia) is present in <10% of cases; sterile pyuria and white blood cell casts are common. EARLY DISCONTINUATION OF INCITING DRUG COMBINED WITH EARLY ORAL CORTICOSTEROIDS (Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day within 7-14 days) prevents irreversible interstitial fibrosis.
patient_plain_language: An allergic reaction deep inside the sponge tissue surrounding your kidney tubes (interstitium) caused by a medication—most commonly everyday heartburn pills (Prilosec/Nexium), pain relievers (ibuprofen/Advil), or antibiotics. White blood cells swarm into your kidneys, causing inflammation and kidney failure. Stopping the offending pill immediately and taking a short course of steroid pills heals the kidneys and prevents permanent scarring.

name: Myasthenia Gravis (AChR-Ab Post-Synaptic Junction Failure)
overview: Myasthenia Gravis involves pathogenic autoantibodies (anti-AChR in 85%, anti-MuSK, anti-LRP4) blocking and destroying post-synaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, producing hallmark FATIGABLE muscle weakness (worsens with repetitive use, improves with rest). The phase 3 ADAPT trial (n=167) proved that neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) blocker EFGARTIGIMOD produced rapid, significant clinical improvement (68% responders vs 30% placebo; p<0.0001). Pyridostigmine provides symptomatic acetylcholinesterase inhibition; thymectomy is class I recommendation in non-thymomatous generalized AChR+ MG.
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where your immune system attacks the docking docks (acetylcholine receptors) on your muscle cells. Nerves can send signals, but the muscles cannot catch them. This causes hallmark 'fatigue weakness': your eyelids droop (ptosis), your vision goes double, and chewing or walking gets progressively weaker as the day goes on, but temporarily improves after a rest nap.

name: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS - Pre-Synaptic P/Q-Type VGCC)
alternative_names: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome (LEMS - Pre-Synaptic P/Q-Type VGCC)
overview: Unlike Myasthenia Gravis, LEMS involves autoantibodies directed against PRE-SYNAPTIC P/Q-type Voltage-Gated Calcium Channels (VGCC), blocking calcium influx and preventing acetylcholine vesicle release. OVER 50-60% OF PATIENTS HAVE SMALL CELL LUNG CANCER (SCLC - Paraneoplastic LEMS). Clinical hallmark: PROXIMAL MUSCLE STRENGTH AND DEEP TENDON REFLEXES TEMPORARILY IMPROVE FOLLOWING BRIEF MAXIMUM EXERCISE (POST-EXERCISE FACILITATION). AMIFAMPRIDINE (3,4-diaminopyridine / 3,4-DAP) blocks potassium channels, prolonging nerve depolarization and restoring muscle strength (p<0.001).
patient_plain_language: A rare condition where antibodies block the microscopic calcium gates at the very tips of your nerves, preventing them from releasing the chemical that tells muscles to contract. Over half of patients have a hidden small cell lung tumor producing these antibodies. Unlike myasthenia gravis, your muscle strength actually feels STRONGER for a few seconds right after a short burst of exercise (post-exercise facilitation). A targeted pill (Amifampridine) restores nerve firing.

name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS - Mixed Upper & Lower Motor Neuron)
alternative_names: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS - Mixed Upper & Lower Motor Neuron)
overview: ALS is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder causing relentless loss of both Upper Motor Neurons (hyperreflexia, spasticity, positive Babinski sign) and Lower Motor Neurons (fasciculations, muscle atrophy, flaccid weakness). RILUZOLE (50 mg BID oral glutamatergic inhibitor) extends tracheostomy-free survival by 2-3 months. IV/oral EDARAVONE (Radicava; free radical scavenger) slows functional decline by 33% on the ALSFRS-R scale in early definite ALS (p=0.001). EARLY NON-INVASIVE VENTILATION (NIV/BiPAP for FVC <50-80%) extends survival by 7-12 months and preserves quality of life.
patient_plain_language: A motor neuron disease (often known as Lou Gehrig's disease) where the nerve cells that control your voluntary muscles gradually waste away. Because both upper nerves in the brain and lower nerves in the spinal cord are affected, it causes a combination of muscle twitching (fasciculations), shrinking (atrophy), and muscle stiffness. Multidisciplinary ALS clinic care, early nighttime breathing support (BiPAP), and protective medicines (Riluzole and Radicava) prolong survival and comfort.

name: Guillain-Barré Syndrome (Acute Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy)
overview: GBS is an acute autoimmune post-infectious demyelinating polyneuropathy (commonly following Campylobacter jejuni, CMV, or respiratory illness) presenting with RAPIDLY ASCENDING SYMMETRICAL FLACCID PARALYSIS, AREFLEXIA, and autonomic instability. CORTICOSTEROIDS ARE COMPLETELY INEFFECTIVE AND HARMFUL. INTRAVENOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN (IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) OR THERAPEUTIC PLASMA EXCHANGE (PE 4-5 sessions) initiated within 2 weeks halts progression and significantly accelerates motor recovery.
patient_plain_language: A rapid, temporary immune reaction (often triggered by a stomach bug or cold 1 to 3 weeks earlier) where your immune system attacks the insulation (myelin) covering your peripheral nerves. Weakness starts in your toes and legs and climbs upward toward your chest, along with numbness and loss of reflexes. Corticosteroids do NOT work; emergency hospital care with IV antibody infusions (IVIG) or plasma filtering clears the attack while nerves heal.

name: Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP)
overview: CIDP is a chronic, progressive or relapsing-remitting symmetric sensorimotor polyradiculoneuropathy progressing for >8 WEEKS (differentiating it from acute GBS). Unlike GBS, CIDP RESPONDS WELL TO CORTICOSTEROIDS. The phase 3 PATH trial (n=245) proved that weekly SUB-CUTANEOUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN (SCIG 0.2 g/kg or 0.4 g/kg) achieved 67-78% relapse-free survival compared to 37% placebo (p=0.0007), providing convenient at-home maintenance.
patient_plain_language: A chronic, ongoing autoimmune condition where your immune system continuously damages the insulation around your nerves over months or years. Unlike GBS which strikes suddenly and heals, CIDP slowly causes weakness and numbness in both legs and arms that lasts longer than 2 months. Fortunately, CIDP responds very well to regular antibody infusions (IVIG or easy at-home under-the-skin SCIG) or steroid pills.

name: Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux - Neurovascular Compression)
overview: Classic TN involves paroxysmal, excruciating, electric shock-like lancinating unilateral facial pain in V2/V3 distributions, triggered by innocuous tactile stimuli (touching face, brushing teeth, chewing, breeze). Caused by neurovascular compression of the trigeminal root entry zone (most commonly superior cerebellar artery). CARBAMAZEPINE (200-1200 mg/day) or OXCARBAZEPINE is first-line medical therapy, achieving initial pain relief in >80%. MICROVASCULAR DECOMPRESSION (MVD / Jannetta procedure) provides definitive cure (>70-80% pain-free at 10 years).
patient_plain_language: Known as one of the most agonizing pains in human medicine ('Tic Douloureux'). An artery at the base of your brain pulses against your trigeminal facial nerve like a hammer on an exposed electrical wire. The slightest light touch—a cool breeze, brushing your teeth, or chewing—triggers lightning bolts of excruciating electrical pain shooting across your cheek or jaw. A specific nerve pill (Carbamazepine) or a keyhole brain surgery to pad the nerve (MVD) stops the pain completely.

name: Sjögren's Disease (Anti-SSA/Ro Autoimmune Exocrinopathy)
overview: Sjögren's is a systemic autoimmune exocrinopathy characterized by lymphocytic infiltration of salivary and lacrimal glands, producing Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca (severe dry eyes) and Xerostomia (severe dry mouth). Autoantibodies (Anti-SSA/Ro in 70-80%, Anti-SSB/La) are diagnostic. SJÖGREN'S CARRIES A 15-TO-40-FOLD ELEVATED RISK OF NON-HODGKIN B-CELL LYMPHOMA (MALT lymphoma of the parotid). Muscarinic agonists (Pilocarpine, Cevimeline) stimulate secretion; Hydroxychloroquine treats systemic arthralgias.
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where your immune cells attack and dry out the moisture-producing glands in your body, particularly your tear glands and salivary glands. Your eyes feel like they are full of sandpaper or grit, and your mouth becomes so dry you cannot swallow dry crackers without water. Because saliva protects your teeth, aggressive dental care is critical, and doctors must monitor for swollen parotid glands to screen for lymphoma.

name: Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (Anti-Scl-70 / Scleroderma Renal Crisis)
alternative_names: Diffuse Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (Anti-Scl-70 / Scleroderma Renal Crisis)
overview: Diffuse systemic sclerosis causes widespread skin fibrosis proximal to elbows/knees, driven by vasculopathy and autoantibodies (Anti-Scl-70 / Topoisomerase I in 30%, Anti-RNA Polymerase III). Anti-RNA Polymerase III carries high risk for SCLERODERMA RENAL CRISIS (SRC: acute malignant hypertension, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and oliguric AKI). ACE INHIBITORS (CAPTOPRIL TITRATED AGGRESSIVELY) ARE LIFE-SAVING FOR SRC. CORTICOSTEROIDS (PREDNISONE >15 MG/DAY) DIRECTLY PRECIPITATE RENAL CRISIS AND ARE STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED.
patient_plain_language: A serious autoimmune condition where your body overproduces collagen scar tissue throughout your skin and internal organs. The skin on your fingers, arms, chest, and face becomes tight, shiny, and hard like leather. It can cause blood vessel spasms (Raynaud's), heartburn, lung scarring, and sudden kidney crises. Steroids are dangerous poisons in this condition because they trigger kidney failure, but blood pressure pills (Captopril) protect your kidneys.

name: Limited Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (CREST Syndrome / Anti-Centromere)
alternative_names: Limited Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (CREST Syndrome / Anti-Centromere)
overview: Limited cutaneous SSc is defined by skin thickening restricted to hands, face, and distal extremities, characterized by the classic CREST SYNDROME: Calcinosis cutis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasia. Strongly associated with ANTI-CENTROMERE ANTIBODIES (ACA in >70-80%). Unlike diffuse SSc, limited SSc has low risk of renal crisis or severe ILD, but carries a high 10-15% cumulative risk of LATE-ONSET PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (PAH). ANNUAL SCREENING WITH ECHOCARDIOGRAM, DLCO, AND THE DETECT ALGORITHM IS MANDATORY.
patient_plain_language: A milder, slower-moving form of scleroderma often called CREST syndrome. Skin thickening is limited to your fingers and face. The 5 hallmark signs are: calcium lumps under the skin, cold white fingers in the cold (Raynaud's), heartburn difficulty swallowing, claw-like finger tightening (sclerodactyly), and red spider spots on your lips and palms (telangiectasias). The main long-term danger is developing high blood pressure in your lungs (PAH), so a yearly heart ultrasound is essential.

name: Ankylosing Spondylitis (Axial Spondyloarthritis - HLA-B27 Bamboo Spine)
alternative_names: Ankylosing Spondylitis (Axial Spondyloarthritis - HLA-B27 Bamboo Spine)
overview: Axial spondyloarthritis is characterized by immune inflammation of the sacroiliac joints (sacroiliitis) and spine, driven by HLA-B27 and the IL-23/IL-17 pathway, causing syndesmophyte formation and spinal fusion ('Bamboo Spine'). Hallmark: INFLAMMATORY BACK PAIN (onset age <40, insidious onset, IMPROVES WITH EXERCISE, WORSENS WITH REST, nocturnal back pain). CONTINUOUS NSAIDs (Celecoxib, Naproxen) are first-line; Biologics (TNF INHIBITORS like Adalimumab/Infliximab or IL-17 INHIBITORS like Secukinumab/Ixekizumab) achieve ASAS40 response in >60% and arrest radiographic spinal progression.
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune arthritis that attacks your lower back and pelvic joints (sacroiliac joints), strongly linked to the HLA-B27 gene. Unlike common mechanical back pain, this pain is worst in the morning with stiffness lasting over 30 minutes, feels BETTER when you walk or exercise, and wakes you up in the second half of the night. If untreated, bones in the spine fuse together like solid bamboo. Daily stretching, anti-inflammatory pills, and biologic injections keep your spine flexible.

name: Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR - Rapid Low-Dose Corticosteroid Response)
alternative_names: Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR - Rapid Low-Dose Corticosteroid Response)
overview: PMR occurs almost exclusively in adults aged >50, presenting with sudden-onset bilateral aching and severe morning stiffness (>45 minutes) in the shoulder and pelvic girdles, accompanied by marked elevation in ESR (>40-50 mm/h) and CRP. Hallmark: DRAMATIC CLINICAL RESPONSE WITHIN 48-72 HOURS TO LOW-DOSE ORAL PREDNISONE (12.5-20 mg/day; failure to improve within 72 hours strongly suggests an alternative diagnosis). PMR is tightly linked with GIANT CELL ARTERITIS (GCA; co-occurs in 15-20%; temporal artery evaluation mandatory).
patient_plain_language: An inflammatory condition that strikes adults over age 50, causing severe stiffness and aching in both shoulders, neck, and hips. In the morning, you may feel so stiff you cannot raise your arms to brush your hair or put on a coat, or get out of a low chair. It is famous for how quickly it responds: taking a modest dose of Prednisone steroid pills melts the pain away within 48 to 72 hours like magic.

name: Dermatomyositis (Gottron's Papules & Paraneoplastic Myopathy)
overview: Dermatomyositis is an immune-mediated necrotizing microangiopathy of skin and skeletal muscle. Pathognomonic cutaneous hallmarks: HELIOTROPE RASH (violaceous periorbital edema) and GOTTRON'S PAPULES (violaceous scaly plaques over dorsal MCP and PIP joints), accompanied by symmetric proximal muscle weakness (difficulty climbing stairs, combing hair) and elevated Creatine Kinase (CK). OVER 20-30% OF ADULT CASES ARE PARANEOPLASTIC (anti-TIF1-gamma and anti-NXP2 carry high malignancy risk). The landmark ProDERM trial (n=95) proved that IVIG (2 g/kg monthly) achieved 79% significant clinical response versus 44% placebo (p=0.006).
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune condition where your immune system attacks your small blood vessels, causing inflammation in your skin and muscles. It causes a distinctive purplish rash over your eyelids (heliotrope rash) and red, scaly bumps across your knuckles (Gottron's papules), along with weakness in your shoulders and thighs. Because it is frequently triggered by a hidden cancer, thorough full-body cancer screening is mandatory.

name: Bullous Pemphigoid (BP180/BP230 Subepidermal Tense Blisters)
overview: Bullous pemphigoid is the most common autoimmune blistering disease, predominantly affecting elderly individuals (>70 years), frequently linked to neurological comorbidities (dementia, Parkinson's) or DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins). Pathogenic autoantibodies target hemidesmosomal adhesion proteins BP180 and BP230 at the dermal-epidermal junction. Produces TENSE SUBEPIDERMAL BULLAE ON ERYTHEMATOUS BASES WITH NEGATIVE NIKOLSKY SIGN. HIGH-POTENCY TOPICAL CORTICOSTEROIDS (Clobetasol propionate cream 20-30 g/day) are EQUALLY EFFECTIVE TO ORAL STEROIDS WITH SIGNIFICANTLY LOWER 1-YEAR MORTALITY (Lancet landmark trial).
patient_plain_language: An autoimmune blistering disease of older adults where antibodies attack the microscopic velcro anchors (hemidesmosomes) that hold the outer layer of skin to the bottom layer. Because the split is deep, it causes thick, taut, dome-shaped blisters ('tense bullae') that do not pop easily, often starting with intense itching. Rubbing high-strength steroid cream (Clobetasol) all over the skin heals the blisters just as well as steroid pills with far fewer side effects.

name: Pemphigus Vulgaris (Desmoglein 3/1 Intraepidermal Flaccid Blisters)
overview: Pemphigus vulgaris is a potentially fatal intraepidermal blistering disorder caused by IgG autoantibodies targeting desmoglein 3 (mucosal-predominant) and desmoglein 1 (mucocutaneous). Produces ACANTHOLYSIS (loss of keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte cell adhesion), resulting in FLACCID BLISTERS THAT RUPTURE EASILY, extensive painful oral erosions, and POSITIVE NIKOLSKY SIGN (slight friction dislodges skin). The landmark Ritux 3 trial (n=90) proved that FIRST-LINE RITUXIMAB (1,000 mg Day 1 and 15) COMBINED WITH SHORT-TERM PREDNISONE achieved complete remission off therapy in 89% vs 34% prednisone alone (p<0.0001), establishing Rituximab as the global gold standard.
patient_plain_language: A rare, serious autoimmune skin disease where your antibodies attack the glue (desmoglein) that binds skin cells together. Because the breakdown happens inside the top layer of skin, blisters are thin, floppy ('flaccid'), and burst almost immediately, leaving raw, painful weeping red sores that look like severe burns. It almost always begins with agonizing sores inside your mouth. Targeted Rituximab antibody infusions cure the disease in nearly 90% of patients.

name: Multiple Myeloma (CRAB Criteria & Quadruplet Induction GDMT)
alternative_names: Multiple Myeloma (CRAB Criteria & Quadruplet Induction GDMT)
overview: Multiple myeloma is a clonal plasma cell malignancy producing monoclonal immunoglobulin and end-organ damage (the CRAB CRITERIA: Hypercalcemia, Renal insufficiency, Anemia, Bone lytic lesions; or SLiM biomarkers: >=60% marrow plasma cells, serum free light chain ratio >=100, >1 focal MRI lesion). The phase 2/3 GRIFFIN trial (n=207) established that QUADRUPLET INDUCTION (Daratumumab + Bortezomib + Lenalidomide + Dexamethasone / D-VRd) achieved significantly higher Stringent Complete Response (62.6% vs 45.4%; p=0.018) and MRD-negativity rates.
patient_plain_language: A blood cancer where abnormal plasma cells (which normally make infection-fighting antibodies) multiply uncontrollably in your bone marrow. They dissolve holes in your bones ('punched-out lesions'), spill toxic light chain proteins that clog your kidneys, cause anemia, and spike blood calcium. Breakthrough 4-drug combination therapy (including targeted antibody Daratumumab) knocks the cancer into deep remission, followed by a stem cell transplant.

name: Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS - Premalignant)
alternative_names: Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS - Premalignant)
overview: MGUS is an asymptomatic premalignant plasma cell precursor condition present in >3-5% of adults over 50. Defined by: 1) Serum monoclonal protein (M-protein) <30 g/L (<3.0 g/dL); 2) Clonal bone marrow plasma cells <10%; 3) ABSOLUTE ABSENCE OF END-ORGAN DAMAGE (NO CRAB FEATURES: normal calcium, normal renal function, normal hemoglobin, and absence of lytic bone lesions on skeletal imaging). Progresses to multiple myeloma or related disorders at a constant rate of 1% per year. MANAGEMENT IS STRICT OBSERVATION (WATCH-AND-WAIT); CHEMOTHERAPY OR IMMUNOTHERAPY IS STRICTLY HARMFUL.
patient_plain_language: A common, silent blood finding where a small cluster of plasma cells produces a small amount of extra antibody protein (M-spike) in your blood. It is NOT active cancer and causes ZERO symptoms, zero bone damage, and zero kidney damage. Over 99% of people live completely normal lifespans with no issues. The risk of it ever turning into active myeloma is only about 1% per year, so no treatment or chemo is needed—just a simple yearly blood check.

name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL - Del(17p)/TP53 & BTK Inhibitors)
alternative_names: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL - Del(17p)/TP53 & BTK Inhibitors)
overview: CLL is a clonal proliferation of mature CD5+/CD19+/CD23+ B-cells. Asymptomatic early stage (Rai 0 / Binet A) requires observation ('watch and wait'). For symptomatic or high-risk disease (del(17p) or TP53 mutation, which confers chemo-refractory biology), TARGETED CHEMO-FREE GDMT IS MANDATORY. name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML - Auer Rods & Targeted 7+3 Induction)
alternative_names: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML - Auer Rods & Targeted 7+3 Induction)
overview: AML is an aggressive hematologic emergency characterized by clonal expansion of poorly differentiated myeloid precursors (blasts >=20% in bone marrow/blood) with presence of AUER RODS on microscopy. In fit younger patients, intensive '7+3' induction (Cytarabine 7 days + Daunorubicin 3 days) combined with targeted agents (Midostaurin for FLT3-mutated; Gemtuzumab ozogamicin for CD33+) is standard. In unfit or older patients (>=75 years), the landmark VIALE-A trial (n=431) revolutionized therapy: AZACITIDINE + BCL-2 INHIBITOR VENETOCLAX significantly prolonged overall survival (14.7 vs 9.6 months; hazard ratio 0.66; p<0.001) and doubled complete remission rates (66.4% vs 28.3%).
patient_plain_language: An aggressive, fast-moving cancer of the blood where your bone marrow fills with immature, non-working white blood cells called myeloblasts. Because blasts crowd out normal cells, you rapidly become severely anemic, vulnerable to life-threatening infections, and bleed easily. For patients who cannot handle intense hospital chemotherapy, modern combination therapy using Azacitidine with a targeted pill called Venetoclax produces dramatic remissions.

name: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma (Reed-Sternberg Cells & Nivolumab-AVD)
overview: Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma (cHL) is characterized by giant multinucleated REED-STERNBERG CELLS (CD30+, CD15+) surrounded by an extensive reactive inflammatory background, frequently presenting in adolescents and young adults with painless rubbery cervical lymphadenopathy and B-symptoms (fever, drenching night sweats, weight loss). patient_plain_language: A highly curable cancer of the lymphatic system that most often affects teenagers and young adults. It begins as a painless, rubbery lump in your neck or collarbone, sometimes with drenching night sweats and fevers. Under a microscope, pathognomonic giant cancer cells look like owl eyes (Reed-Sternberg cells). Modern treatment combining immunotherapy (Nivolumab) with chemotherapy cures over 94% of patients while protecting nerves and fertility.

name: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL - Pola-R-CHP & CAR-T Therapy)
alternative_names: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL - Pola-R-CHP & CAR-T Therapy)
overview: DLBCL is the most common aggressive Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma, characterized by diffuse sheets of large atypical CD20+ B-cells with high proliferative index (Ki-67 >70-80%). The landmark phase 3 POLARIX trial (n=879) proved that replacing vincristine with antibody-drug conjugate Polatuzumab Vedotin (Pola-R-CHP: Polatuzumab + Rituximab + Cyclophosphamide + Doxorubicin + Prednisone) achieved a 27% reduction in risk of progression, relapse, or death compared to standard R-CHOP (p=0.02). In primary refractory or early relapsed DLBCL (<=12 months), CD19 CAR T-CELL THERAPY (Axicabtagene ciloleucel; ZUMA-7 trial) quadrupled 2-year event-free survival (40.5% vs 16.3%; p<0.001) over autologous stem cell transplant.
patient_plain_language: The most common aggressive lymphoma in adults. Although fast-growing, it is highly curable with intensive treatment. Modern frontline therapy uses an antibody-drug smart bomb (Polatuzumab) combined with chemo (Pola-R-CHP). If the lymphoma ever returns, miraculous living cell therapy (CAR-T cells), where your own immune cells are genetically re-engineered to hunt down and kill cancer cells, cures over 40% of relapsed patients.
